dispositions.topic_text: Required consistency among each owner audit action, its table-row subject kind, M09 mapping, M15–M19 payload form, invariant, and test
dispositions.what: A check over the release's data that every row of OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS has the subject_kind whose AuditSubject variant M09 fixes for that row's audit_action, and that an entry appended for the row carries that variant (M15-M19); a row that disagrees fails the check.
keeps:
- the subject, by identity only (R0-37), one of a closed set fixed by the
  action (owner, 2026-10-31; codex round-02 T4): the project (`project_id`)
  for a project's actions; the customer (`customer_ref`) for a customer's
  actions, restricting and lifting, ending and resuming; the session and the
  project for a grant or a revocation; for the import, the digest of the file
  it accepted (M10) — the migration closure is unique in the instance and has
  no other identity (codex round-04 T1); none for an erasure of old entries,
  whose fact is the owner's date;
options: Make row-key coverage, audit-action mapping, subject-kind mapping, and the written entry's M15–M19 subject payload one invariant, with mismatched releases inadmissible.
Require the row's subject kind to agree with M09 while deriving entry subjects independently from M09.
Treat the row's subject kind as authoritative even when it disagrees with M09.
consequences: Without a consistency invariant and a Required test that shows it, a mismatched release may either be rejected or admit an accepted action whose audit subject has the wrong identity form; treating the row as authoritative without requiring agreement breaks M09.
